name: Polyglucosan Body Myopathy Type 1

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Polyglucosan Body Myopathy Type 1

criteria.description: Adult-onset progressive distal and proximal muscle weakness with variable sensory neuropathy
Presence of polyglucosan bodies on muscle biopsy with periodic acid–Schiff (PAS) positive inclusions
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the RBCK1 gene
Electromyography showing myopathic changes with or without neuropathic features
Exclusion of other causes of myopathy and neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of adult-onset progressive muscle weakness, polyglucosan bodies on muscle biopsy, and pathogenic RBCK1 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histopathological, and genetic findings.

pathognomonic.notes: Detected by PAS staining on muscle biopsy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Adult-onset distal and proximal muscle weakness
searchTerms: muscle weakness starting in arms and legs
weakness in nearby and far muscles
progressive nerve damage affecting movement and sensation
loss of feeling and strength in limbs

common.symptomName: Muscle atrophy predominantly in distal limbs
searchTerms: muscle wasting in hands and feet
loss of muscle bulk in arms and legs

common.symptomName: Gait disturbance due to distal weakness
searchTerms: difficulty walking due to weak legs

common.symptomName: Mild sensory loss in distal extremities
searchTerms: mild numbness in hands and feet
slight loss of feeling in fingers and toes

occasional.notes: May include arrhythmias or heart block

rare.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness leading to dyspnea
searchTerms: breathing difficulty from weak respiratory muscles
shortness of breath due to muscle weakness

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate)
Normal to mildly elevated inflammatory markers
imaging: Muscle MRI showing fatty infiltration and atrophy in distal and proximal muscles
Cardiac MRI may reveal fibrosis or cardiomyopathy
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating PAS-positive polyglucosan bodies
Electromyography showing myopathic and neuropathic features

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent central nervous system involvement
Predominantly neuropathic symptoms without polyglucosan bodies
Lack of muscle biopsy PAS-positive inclusions

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness with respiratory compromise
Cardiac arrhythmias or conduction block in a patient with myopathy
Early onset severe neuropathy with cognitive decline
references: Schweizer et al., 'Polyglucosan Body Myopathy Type 1: Clinical and Genetic Features', Neurology, 2022
Orphanet Report on Polyglucosan Body Myopathy Type 1, 2023
